PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior with one clear Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single responsibility makes failures easier to diagnose. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if exactly one scenario/one Act; non-compliant if multiple Acts or multiple unrelated behaviors. DECISION RULES: (1) Count distinct Act operations: the test calls tabelaHash0.insere(...) twice (two Act invocations). (2) Name does not indicate multiple operations. (3) There are multiple assertion groups validating distinct outcomes tied to duplicate-insert behavior. Given the presence of multiple Act invocations for the scenario, and per the decision rules, verdict is non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not depend on other tests and should be isolated. RATIONALE: Enables independent execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if local variables only or proper setup/teardown used. DECISION RULES: (1) No @Before/@After in visible snippet but the test uses only local variables (tabelaHash0, object0). (2) No static or instance mutable state is modified in the method. Given the method uses only local state and no evidence of shared mutable state, verdict is compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Provide tests for happy path and error scenarios. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if there are at least two tests per method: one happy and one error/exceptional. DECISION RULES: (1) The class as shown has a single test method covering a happy path (duplicate insert scenario). (2) No assertThrows, @Test(expected=...), or tests named with 'invalid'/'exception'. (3) With only one test visible, there is no evidence of error-case coverage. Verdict: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should check boundary and edge values. RATIONALE: Many bugs appear at boundaries. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if test data includes empty string, zero, negative, MAX_VALUE, etc. DECISION RULES: (1) The test uses a special key constant (KEY_SPECIAL) and a regular object; there are no empty/zero/negative/long-value checks. (2) No method names indicate boundary testing. (3) The domain (hash table) can have boundaries but the test does not exercise them. Verdict: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Extract repeated setup into helpers and avoid duplication. RATIONALE: Improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if helper methods or constants are used; non-compliant if code is duplicated or magic values used. DECISION RULES: (1) No private helper methods or constants are visible in the test method. (2) The method repeats object creation and insertion inline. Given absence of helper extraction and inline setup, verdict is non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and avoid loops/complex conditionals. RATIONALE: Easier to reason about and maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if method <20 lines, no loops/complex conditionals. DECISION RULES: (1) The test method is short and linear (<20 lines). (2) No loops, conditionals, or complex control flow. Given the method is compact and simple, verdict is compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple relevant properties. RATIONALE: Deeper assertions catch more faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if multiple properties are asserted (e.g., result identity, items length, contents). DECISION RULES: (1) The test asserts pesquisa result, items not null, items length, and stored item identity (multiple assertions). Given multiple targeted assertions, verdict is compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored/commented-out tests. RATIONALE: Keeps suite actionable. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if there are no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test. DECISION RULES: (1) No @Ignore/@Disabled present in snippet. (2) No commented-out tests observed. Given all tests are active, verdict is compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should reference requirements. RATIONALE: Facilitates traceability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if annotations or Javadoc mention requirement IDs. DECISION RULES: (1) Class Javadoc explicitly contains 'Requirement trace: REQ-001'. Given that explicit requirement trace is present, verdict is compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests are separate. RATIONALE: Non-functional tests need dedicated handling. EVALUATION CRITERIA: usually not-applicable for unit tests unless explicit performance/security assertions exist. DECISION RULES: (1) No explicit performance or security tests are present despite a @Test(timeout=...). This is a unit functional test; per the evaluation rules this practice is generally not-applicable. VERDICT: not-applicable.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome. RATIONALE: Improves readability and debugging. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if names follow descriptive patterns; non-compliant if generic names like test7. DECISION RULES: (1) The method name is 'test7', which is generic and non-descriptive. (2) Although comments exist, the method name does not document scenario/expected result. Verdict: non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should verify public behavior via public APIs and avoid testing internals. RATIONALE: Reduces brittleness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if only public methods are used and no reflection. DECISION RULES: (1) The test calls public API methods (insere, pesquisa, recuperaItens) and uses no reflection or private-field access. Verdict: compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Use specific assertions and include descriptive messages. RATIONALE: Useful messages and specific assertions aid debugging. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if assertions use assertEquals/assertSame with messages. DECISION RULES: (1) The test uses assertSame, assertNotNull, assertEquals with descriptive messages on several assertions. Majority of assertions include messages, so verdict is compliant. PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why' not 'what' and be minimal. RATIONALE: Useful comments help maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if code has concise, meaningful comments and no commented-out code. DECISION RULES: (1) The method contains Given-When-Then comments and class-level Javadoc; no commented-out code. Verdict: compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be deterministic and avoid random/time/external dependencies. RATIONALE: Prevent flaky tests. DECISION RULES: (1) The test uses only local deterministic operations and no random/time calls or sleeps; no external service invocation is visible. Verdict: compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should not create lasting side-effects or depend on cleanup. RATIONALE: Avoid test interdependence and resource leaks.
